The '''2018–19 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arizona]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by 10th-year head coach [[Sean Miller]] and played their home games at [[McKale Center]] in [[Tucson, Arizona]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. They finished the season 17–15, 8–10 in [[2018–19 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in three-way tie for 6th place. They received the 9-seed in the [[2019 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2019 Pac-12 tournament]], where they lost to 8-seed [[2018–19 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] in the first round, 78–65.

==Previous season==
{{main|2017–18 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal}}

assistant basketball coach Book Richardson after his appeal fails|last=Schmidt|first=Caitlin|work=Tucson.com|access-date=2018-01-25|language=en}}</ref>

On February 23, 2018, according to a published report by ESPN, an FBI wiretap revealed that head coach [[Sean Miller]] talked with Christian Dawkins (another key figure in the scandal) to discuss paying their top prospect, [[Deandre Ayton]], $100,000 to commit to Arizona, with the monetary situation being dealt with directly with him.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22559284/sean-miller-arizona-christian-dawkins-discussed-payment-ensure-deandre-ayton-signing-according-fbi-investigation|title=FBI wiretaps show Sean Miller discussed $100K payment to lock recruit|last=Schlabach|first=Mark|date=February 23, 2018|website=www.espn.com|publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> While Miller would not coach their next game that day against Oregon, Arizona allowed Ayton to play.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22567552/sean-miller-coach-arizona-wildcats-saturday-oregon-ducks|title=Sean Miller won't coach Arizona's game Saturday vs. Oregon|date=February 24, 2018|website=www.espn.com |publisher=ESPN |access-date=February 24, 2018}}</ref> Coach Sean Miller subsequently denied the allegation and the University of Arizona announced he will remain the coach of Arizona Wildcats men’s basketball team, with Ayton also allowed to continue playing with the team for the rest of the season. However, as a consequence of the report involving Ayton, both of Arizona's remaining committed recruits from the class of 2018, [[Shareef O'Neal]] and Brandon Williams, announced they had decommitted.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/03/sean-miller-deandre-ayton-arizona-nba-draft | title=Sean Miller: Deandre Ayton will declare for NBA draft }}</ref>

During the season, Arizona defeated [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the Valley of the Sun Shootout in [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix, AZ]]. Arizona also defeated the same [[2017–18 UMBC Retrievers men's basketball team|UMBC team]] that would go on to a [[2018 UMBC vs. Virginia men's basketball game|historic upset]] of top-ranked [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the NCAA tournament. Arizona lost to [[2017–18 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]], [[2017–18 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]] and [[2017–18 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] in the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] in [[Nassau, Bahamas|The Bahamas]].

They finished the season 27–8, 14–4 in [[2017–18 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 play]] to finish in a first place. The championship marked the school's 16th Pac-12 regular season championship title (back to back, 29th overall). As the No. 1 seed in the [[2018 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], Arizona defeated [[2017–18 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], [[2017–18 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]] (avenged from 82–74 loss on February 4 in Tucson, AZ) and [[2017–18 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]] to win the 2nd straight Pac-12 tournament championship title for the 7th time. As a result, the Wildcats received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the sixth consecutive year (35th NCAA tournament appearances). As a No. 4 seed in the South region, in the First round, they lost to No. 13 seed [[2017–18 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]] 89–68.

He backed out of his commitment to Arizona after more information relating to the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]] came out (similar to former Arizona commit [[Shareef O'Neal]]), but he ultimately decided to stay with Arizona on May 5, 2018.

===2019 recruiting class===
[[Nico Mannion]], originally from [[Siena]], [[Italy]], was originally a part of the 2020 recruiting class, but [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2019 class in July 2018. He verbally committed to Arizona on September 14, 2018, over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]]. Mannion is a consensus five-star prospect out of [[Pinnacle High School|Pinnacle HS]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]].

[[Christian Koloko]], originally from [[Doula]], [[Cameroon]], was the second commitment in the Arizona class. He committed to Arizona on September 23, 2018, over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. He is a consensus three-star prospect out of [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]].

[[Josh Green (basketball)|Josh Green]], originally from [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], [[Australia]] was the third commitment in the Arizona’s 2019 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on October 4, 2018, over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] and [[UNLV Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]]. Green is a consensus five-star prospect out of [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].

[[Zeke Nnaji]], originally from [[Lakeville, Minnesota|Lakeville, MN]] was the fifth commitment in the Arizona’s 2019 recruiting class. He verbally committed to Arizona on November 23, 2018, over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], North Carolina, Kansas and [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]]. Nnaji is a consensus four-star prospect out of [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]].

== Preseason ==

=== Red and Blue game ===
The annual Red-Blue game will take place at McKale Center on October 14, 2018. After sophomore Brandon Randolph defended his crown in the dunk contest,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2018/10/14/mens-basketball-randolph-wins-slam-dunk-title-red-team-claims-victory.aspx|title=Randolph Wins Slam Dunk Title, Red Team Claims Victory|date=14 October 2018|accessdate=22 October 2018}}</ref> the Red team, led by Ira Lee, knocked off the Blue team, 39-33.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/documents/2018/10/14//Red_Blue_Box_Score.PDF?id=17118|title=Box Score|date=14 October 2018|accessdate=14 October 2018}}</ref>

=== Preseason rankings ===
The Arizona Wildcats were selected fourth in the 2018-19 Pac-12 media poll.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2018/10/11/oregon-picked-pac-12-mens-basketball-preseason-favorite.aspx|title=Oregon picked as Pac-12 Men's Basketball preseason favorite|date=11 October 2018|website=Pac-12.com|access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref>
On October 22, Arizona began the season unranked receiving 14 votes in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP poll]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.ap.org/poll|title=The AP Top 25 Poll|date=22 October 2018|accessdate=22 October 2018}}</ref>  It was the first time since the [[2010–11 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|2010–11]], began the season not in the AP Poll.

==Schedule and results==
The Wildcats opponents were finalized in the summer and dates and times will be finalized in the fall. Current confirmed opponents are exhibition games against Division II school [[Chaminade University|Chaminade]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]], [[Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball|Houston Baptist]], [[Montana Grizzlies men's basketball|Montana]], [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]], [[UC Davis Aggies men's basketball|UC Davis]], [[UTEP Miners men's basketball|UTEP]] and [[Utah Valley Wolverines men's basketball|Utah Valley]]. They will also participate in the 2018 [[Maui Invitational Tournament]] with three of the following potential opponents including ([[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego]], or [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]]). Arizona has two true away games with [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] at [[Coleman Coliseum]], and [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] at the [[XL Center]].
In the unbalanced 18-game Pac-12 schedule, Arizona will not play the two Washington schools on the road ([[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]]) and two Los Angeles schools at home ([[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]).
